'''Giorgio Salvini''' (24 April 1920 – 8 April 2015) was an Italian physicist and politician.
==Life==
Born in [[Milan]], Salvini was responsible for the construction of the first Italian circular [[particle accelerator]] in 1953, the electron synchrotron of Frascati ("elettrosincrotrone di Frascati").<ref name="bio">{{cite news|last1=Stefano Rizzato|title=È morto Giorgio Salvini, fisico ed ex ministro|url=http://www.lastampa.it/2015/04/08/italia/cronache/morto-giorgio-salvini-fisico-ed-ex-ministro-rhc0ao7AzhfuCTcZGO4A5M/pagina.html|accessdate=7 December 2015|work=[[La Stampa]]|date=8 April 2015}}</ref> Between 1966 and 1970 he was president of the [[Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare]] (INFN).<ref name="bio"/> Salvini took part in the [[CERN]] experiment that led to the discovery of the [[W and Z bosons]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://home.infn.it/en/media-outreach/news/1596-goodbye-to-giorgio-salvini-father-of-the-frascati-laboratories-and-of-the-electron-synchrotron|title=Goodbye to Giorgio Salvini, father of the Frascati Laboratories and of the Electron Synchrotron|last=|first=|date=8 April 2015|website=National Institute for Nuclear Physics|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621110602/https://home.infn.it/en/media-outreach/news/1596-goodbye-to-giorgio-salvini-father-of-the-frascati-laboratories-and-of-the-electron-synchrotron|archive-date=2018-06-21|access-date=2 March 2020}}</ref>

He served as president of the [[Accademia dei Lincei]] from 1990 to 1994.<ref name="bio"/>

He was Minister of University, Scientific Research and Technology in the [[Lamberto Dini|Dini]] [[Dini Cabinet|1995-1996 cabinet]].<ref name="bio"/>
